title: Addition of pointed relative torsor classes under an equivariant pairing
statement: Let T be a scheme, U an object of its small etale site, G an abelian sheaf, and I an injective resolution of G [def-amb-relative-etale-cohomology]. Let P,Q,R be G-torsors, m:P times Q to R a natural pairing equivariant in both inputs, and tau1 in P(U), tau2 in Q(U). Then the raw relativeTorsorEquiv class [lem-amb-relative-cocycle-coordinates] of (R,m(tau1,tau2)) equals the sum of the classes of (P,tau1) and (Q,tau2).

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1, torsors and injective lifting torsors; explicit binary pairing and relative signed-cone refinement.

proof.text: Present P and Q as lifting torsors for the same short exact sequence G to I0 to cycles(I,1). Transport the two specified sections to lifts b1,b2 of global cocycles s1,s2. Their sum b1+b2 lifts s1+s2. In the signed relative cone the cycle has coordinates (iCycles(s),-b); additivity of both coordinates gives additivity of the cycle and of its homology class.

Addition of ambient lifts defines a natural equivariant pairing P times Q to the lifting torsor S of s1+s2. The binary quotient universal property factors this pairing through m as l:R to S. Restricting to local inputs shows that l is equivariant, hence is an isomorphism of torsors. Its value at m(tau1,tau2) is b1+b2.

The pointed isomorphism identifies the output relative class with the sum-frame class computed in the first step. Apply the presentation formula for relativeTorsorEquiv to obtain the asserted equality. The proof works also for an empty site object U, since all formulas are equations in section groups.

proof_origin.place: Tag 03AJ; G2 gives the full local gluing and signed-coordinate argument in Lean.

lean.statement:
theorem relativeTorsorEquiv_add_of_equivariant (T : Scheme.{u}) (U : T.Etale)
    {G : Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}} (I : InjectiveResolution G)
    (P Q R : Sheaf.Torsor G)
    (m : ∀ A, P.sheaf.obj.obj A → Q.sheaf.obj.obj A → R.sheaf.obj.obj A)
    (hn : ∀ {A B} (f : A ⟶ B) x y, R.sheaf.obj.map f (m A x y) =
      m B (P.sheaf.obj.map f x) (Q.sheaf.obj.map f y))
    (h₁ : ∀ A g x y, m A (P.vadd A g x) y = R.vadd A g (m A x y))
    (h₂ : ∀ A g x y, m A x (Q.vadd A g y) = R.vadd A g (m A x y))
    (τ₁ : P.sheaf.obj.obj (op U)) (τ₂ : Q.sheaf.obj.obj (op U)) :
    relativeTorsorEquiv T U I (Quotient.mk _ ⟨R, m (op U) τ₁ τ₂⟩) =
      relativeTorsorEquiv T U I (Quotient.mk _ ⟨P, τ₁⟩) +
      relativeTorsorEquiv T U I (Quotient.mk _ ⟨Q, τ₂⟩)
